description: A decision rule for a model or the harness around it, filed with evidence for whether it holds. Borrowed heuristics are a law, maxim or rule of thumb imported from human systems and tested for transfer; distilled heuristics are synthesized bottom-up from this catalog's own claims, with no outside source. The evidence list is what makes it an entry rather than a quotation: each item is a claim in this catalog and a verdict on what that claim says about it.

ref.description: Stable opaque identifier, assigned by scripts/assign-ids.mjs, never changed or reused. Cite this, not the slug.

statement.description: The heuristic as usually stated, if borrowed; as distilled, if not.

origin.description: For a borrowed heuristic: who said it, where, roughly when, and the human domain it came from. For a distilled one: which claims it was generalized from and why that pattern was worth naming.

transfer.description: Why it should or should not apply to models: the mechanism, not the analogy. Goodhart transfers because of optimisation pressure on a proxy, not because models are people. For a distilled heuristic this is the mechanism the generalization rests on, not a transfer from elsewhere.

provenance.description: borrowed: imported from outside, with its own origin and author -- Goodhart's law, Hyrum's law. distilled: synthesized bottom-up from this catalog's own claims, no eponym, no outside source.

sources.description: Where the heuristic itself is stated or named, for a borrowed one. Evidence about whether it holds for models goes in `evidence`, as claims.

verdict.description: holds: the claim shows the heuristic applying to models. breaks: it shows the heuristic failing. narrows: it holds only under a condition the note states.

evidence_search.description: A record of having looked for evidence either way and not found it. Same role as on techniques.
